title: 2021 Fall AMC 12A Problem 11
statement: Consider two concentric circles of radius \(17\) and \(19.\) The larger circle has a chord, half of which lies inside the smaller circle. What is the length of the chord in the larger circle?

solutions.text:
Let the chord lie at distance \(d\) from the common center. Its total length is \(2\sqrt{361 - d^2},\) and the portion inside the smaller circle has length \(2\sqrt{289 - d^2}.\)

Since half the chord lies inside, \(2\sqrt{289 - d^2} = \tfrac{1}{2}\cdot 2\sqrt{361 - d^2}.\) Squaring gives \(4(289 - d^2) = 361 - d^2,\) so \(3d^2 = 795\) and \(d^2 = 265.\)

The chord length is \(2\sqrt{361 - 265} = 2\sqrt{96} = 8\sqrt{6}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Let the chord be at distance \(d\) from the center. Its half-length is \(\sqrt{19^2 - d^2},\) and the part inside the small circle has half-length \(\sqrt{17^2 - d^2}\)
“Half lies inside” means the inside portion equals half the whole chord: \(2\sqrt{17^2 - d^2} = \sqrt{19^2 - d^2}\)
